Live application logging

Every MixOS app and compd accepts --debug[=LEVEL]. --debug means --debug=debug; the levels are off, error, warn, info, debug and trace. The default baseline is warn, except Email's warn,email=info. Non-empty RUST_LOG supplies the baseline instead. An explicit debug flag selects the initial live level while preserving that baseline for restoration. The last debug flag wins. Flags after -- are preserved for the app's parser.

workshop --debug
email --debug=info
compd kms-live --debug=debug
journalctl -t workshop -f
journalctl -t email -f
journalctl -t compd -f

The journal identifier is always the binary name, even for an app launched under a different Bus service name. A terminal also receives stderr output; without a terminal, stderr is used if journald cannot be installed. A working journal and a non-terminal stderr produce one copy, in the journal.

LevelMixOS cratesOther dependenciesClamped dependencies
offoffoffoff
errorerrorerrorerror
warnwarnwarnwarn
infoinfoinfowarn
debugdebuginfowarn
tracetraceinfowarn

The clamps cover wgpu_core, wgpu_hal, naga, winit, calloop, egui, eframe, hyper, tokio and rustls. An explicit RUST_LOG baseline can use the full filter grammar; restoring it restores its directives exactly.

Switch a running process through <app>.debug.set, and read it through <app>.debug. These are a Bus intent and query, separate from application actions and menus. For example, in Mix:

$body = json_encode({level: "debug"})
send workshop workshop.debug.set body=$body
send workshop workshop.debug
$body = json_encode({on: false})
send workshop workshop.debug.set body=$body

Set accepts exactly one of level or on. {on:true} selects debug; {on:false} restores the recorded baseline. {level:"off"} disables all tracing events; {level:"warn"} selects a plain warn filter, including in Email. Both commands return {level, on, filter, baseline}. on is true when the filter's maximum enabled verbosity is debug or trace. For a custom baseline, filter is the complete authority; level summarises its maximum. Unknown levels, extra fields and malformed requests are refused without changing the active filter. A query takes an empty object.

An app running with --service NAME answers NAME.debug and NAME.debug.set on that service; apps whose discovery uses canonical app names also accept those names. compd keeps the literal command names comp.debug and comp.debug.set under every --bus-service name:

$body = json_encode({level: "trace"})
send "comp-nested" "comp.debug.set" body=$body

Any local or mesh caller may change the level. The setting is live for this process only: it is not saved to SQLite or app settings and resets at restart. Daemons' durable <service>.log properties remain a separate namespace.

Debug events describe Bus commands and their return codes, window and viewport lifecycle, and settings application. compd also records mapping, placement, grab start/end and initial placement configures. Configure streams and motion detail are trace; debug adds no periodic or per-frame events. Disabled debug events do not format a message or write to the journal. Emitted events cost log volume.

Under apps@N, all apps share a systemd unit and its journal rate limit. A chatty app at debug or trace can therefore cause other apps' lines to be dropped. Watch one binary with journalctl -t <binary> -f and restore the baseline when finished. tracing-journald maps tracing DEBUG to journal priority 6 and TRACE to 7; -o json exposes those priorities and event fields.

compd's separate developer logger still uses its existing log_level configuration and stderr drain. The live tracing control does not change that logger.
